channel.title: LC Insight
channel.description: Crypto market news and on-chain analysis.

item.title: How stolen crypto is traced and frozen, and why thieves dump stablecoins fast
item.description: Every blockchain transfer is public, so investigators can follow stolen funds hop by hop. Money can be stopped in two places: stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle can freeze tokens on-chain, and exchanges can lock accounts when stolen funds arrive.

item.title: Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep at a record 70%. Did a fake pollster move the odds?
item.description: Two days before the November 3 vote, Kalshi's market priced Democrats winning both chambers at 70%, up more than 9 points in a month. Ten days earlier, Kalshi had to explain why a fabricated pollster barely moved its election markets.

item.title: Seed phrase and hardware wallet safety: the words that guard your crypto
item.description: Your seed phrase is the master key to your wallet: anyone who sees it can take everything, and if you lose it, nobody can restore it. A hardware wallet keeps keys offline, but only if the phrase stays offline too and the device is genuine.

item.title: Japan crypto rules explained: FSA registration, 95% cold storage and 2x leverage
item.description: Crypto exchanges in Japan must register with the Financial Services Agency under the Payment Services Act, keep at least 95% of customer coins offline, and cap retail leverage at 2x. A 2026 government bill would revise the rules again, borrowing from securities law.

item.title: Bored Apes are down 96% from their record. Which NFT blue chip fell least?
item.description: Most of the famous NFT collections now sit about 90% to 99% below their peak floor prices in ETH, and the marketplaces are closing. CryptoPunks are the exception, at about 76% down.

item.title: South Korea crypto rules explained: cold wallets, bank-held cash and jail terms
item.description: Crypto exchanges in South Korea must register with the Financial Intelligence Unit and, since July 19, 2024, follow the Virtual Asset User Protection Act: customer cash held at banks, most coins in cold wallets, and prison terms for market manipulation.

item.title: How to check and revoke token approvals before an old one drains your wallet
item.description: Look up your wallet address in an approval checker such as Etherscan's Token Approvals page or Revoke.cash, find spenders you no longer use or do not recognize, and revoke them. Each revoke is an on-chain transaction, so it costs a small network fee.

item.title: One address, two exchange hacks: DeepSea traces where this fall's stolen crypto went
item.description: DeepSea says funds from the Bitget and Binance thefts landed at the same address. Its tracker also shows how little of the loot has reached exchanges, and how much is simply sitting still.

item.title: Prediction markets explained: how Kalshi and Polymarket work, and the real risks
item.description: A prediction market lets people trade contracts that pay $1 if an event happens and $0 if it does not, so prices read like odds. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated US exchange; most Polymarket markets settle on chain through the UMA oracle.

item.title: Singapore crypto rules explained: who needs a MAS license, and who won't get one
item.description: Crypto firms serving customers in Singapore need a license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, mainly under the Payment Services Act 2019. Since June 30, 2025, Singapore firms that serve only overseas customers also need a license, and MAS says it will generally not grant one.

item.title: SEC vs. CFTC: who regulates crypto in the US, and where the line now falls
item.description: The SEC oversees crypto that counts as a security, and the CFTC oversees commodities like bitcoin and ether plus derivatives on them. Since March 2026, the two agencies share an interpretation that says most crypto assets are not securities.

item.title: How crypto exchange hacks happen: the weak spot is rarely the key itself
item.description: Most exchange hacks start in hot wallets, the online wallets that pay out withdrawals. Attackers rarely break the cryptography. They get into the systems and people that approve transactions, then rush to swap stablecoins before issuers can freeze them.

item.title: Binance took in 18,435 BTC in two weeks while $6.81 billion in stablecoins walked out
item.description: DeepSea's data shows about $1.5 billion in bitcoin flowing into Binance in early October, just as billions in USDT left. Kraken saw the opposite, and the price fell anyway.

item.title: Doppler's XDP is trending again, with daily volume 95% below launch week. What is it?
item.description: Doppler Finance's XDP token sat fourth on DeepSea's 24-hour trending list late on November 1 (ET), a month after launch. CoinGecko shows it hit a record low on October 30, and DeepSea finds the top 10 wallets hold 95% of supply.

item.title: How crypto liquidations work: why a 10% move can wipe out a 10x trade
item.description: A liquidation is when an exchange force-closes a leveraged trade because losses have eaten through the trader's collateral. It protects the exchange and other traders from debts the trader cannot pay.

item.title: Perpetual futures funding rates explained: how 0.05% can cost 55% a year
item.description: A funding rate is a small payment that traders of perpetual futures make to each other to keep the contract's price close to the real market price. When it is positive, longs pay shorts. When it is negative, shorts pay longs.

item.title: How crypto airdrops work, and how to spot the scams that copy them
item.description: An airdrop is a free drop of tokens to wallets, usually as a reward for early users. Real airdrops never ask for your seed phrase. Most scams instead trick you into signing a transaction on a fake claim site.

item.title: Asian exchanges lost $11.95 billion in three weeks, most of it USDT leaving Binance
item.description: DeepSea's data shows a steady stablecoin exodus from Asian exchanges starting September 28, weeks before Binance was hacked. Western exchanges barely moved, while smaller dollar tokens began to swing.

item.title: 12,562 sells, 10,480 buys: what Asia's crypto influencers really did in early October
item.description: DeepSea's Asian KOL reports show influencer wallets selling more than they bought, a handful of traders taking most of the profit, and a quiet mid-October week on Solana. For followers, that is a warning.

item.title: Concrete's CT token fell 78% in a month. Its vaults still hold $1.2 billion
item.description: Blueprint Finance's vault platform launched CT on September 30. By November 2 the token traded near $0.134, far below its $0.62 high, even though deposits held steady. Insiders and the foundation own 65% of supply, and its launch post gives no unlock dates.

item.title: A 100/100 token with bundlers among its top holders: how to read DeepSea's risk flags
item.description: DeepSea checks every tracked token for holder concentration, thin liquidity, team selling and bundled supply. After October's run of drains and fake apps, here is what those signals mean, with real examples, and why one score is never the whole story.

item.title: Ether ETFs lost a record $1.61 billion in October, wiping out all of 2026's inflows
item.description: US spot ether funds had their worst month since launch, beating November 2025's record outflow. October erased August and September's gains and left the funds slightly negative for the year, while ETH slid to about $2,270.

item.title: Sui promised Hashi in October with $500 million pledged. Its own page still says testnet
item.description: Hashi is Sui's plan to let native bitcoin back loans on Sui. The Sui Foundation said mainnet would go live in October. On November 2, the official Hashi page still read "Now on Sui Testnet".

item.title: BlackRock's BUIDL slips to No. 3 as tokenized Treasuries shrink to $14.2 billion
item.description: BlackRock's on-chain fund held $2.08 billion on November 1, down 7.61% in a month, and now ranks behind Ondo's USDY and Circle's USYC. The whole tokenized Treasury market shrank 3.68%, but holder numbers keep rising.

item.title: MiCA explained: the EU crypto law, CASP licenses, stablecoin rules and key dates
item.description: MiCA is the EU's rulebook for crypto: firms that offer crypto services need a license from a national regulator, and stablecoins face strict reserve and supervision rules. It has applied in full since December 30, 2024, and the last transition window closed on July 1, 2026.

item.title: Base's next upgrade makes blocks 10 times faster. The code says November 5
item.description: Coinbase's layer 2 switched on its Cobalt upgrade on September 30. Next is Denim, which cuts block times from 2 seconds to 200 milliseconds and could break contracts that count time in blocks. Base's code sets November 5, 1:00 p.m. ET, though Base still calls November only a target.

item.title: Brazil's crypto license deadline has passed. From November 6, banks must drop unlicensed firms
item.description: Crypto firms already operating in Brazil had until October 30, 2026, to file for central bank authorization. From November 6, banks and payment firms may no longer deal with unauthorized providers, and late filers get 30 days at most.

item.title: Whales sold $22.8 million of UNI while it rose 7%, and bought LINK and ARB
item.description: Big wallets used the late October bounce to sell, not buy. DeepSea's 7-day data shows whales net selling RLUSD, UNI and PEPE and making only small purchases of LINK and ARB, as bitcoin closed below $78,000 on October 29.

item.title: Hyperliquid's big traders flipped from 4.2x long to net short, then swung back to 86% long
item.description: In mid-October, traders tracked by DeepSea dumped their bullish bets and piled into ETH and BTC shorts worth more than $200 million apiece. Two weeks later they were leaning long again, even as prices kept sliding.

item.title: Beyond Binance: 19 more crypto hacks in October's last 11 days, about $24.6 million lost
item.description: Binance's $6.3 billion breach dominated October, but SlowMist logged 19 other attacks from October 21 to 31, close to two a day. They range from a $7.45 million multisig mistake to supply chain and DNS attacks.

item.title: Asian exchanges lost $2.2 billion in one week, and $2.12 billion of it left Binance
item.description: DeepSea's report for October 12 to 18 shows stablecoins, mostly USDT on Tron, pouring out of Binance while bitcoin flowed in. The same week, hack-linked funds flooded exchange deposit addresses and a few big Hyperliquid traders turned short.

item.title: Smart money net bought $1.09 million of Concrete as it slid 17%. Its top sale: AUSD
item.description: DeepSea's seven-day flow data to November 2 shows tracked smart money wallets building a position in Concrete (CT) while its price fell, and pulling $3.77 million out of the AUSD stablecoin. Selling signals outnumbered buying ones.

item.title: Pump.fun added Monad and TON and is pushing perps. So why is PUMP down 25% since October 12?
item.description: The Solana memecoin app now lets users trade Monad and TON tokens from one USDC balance and is pushing leveraged perps. Its PUMP token kept sliding, and daily revenue fell about 35% in 11 days.

item.title: How 99 requests to withdraw zero drained 97 million CORE ($1.47 million) from b14g
item.description: A new wallet asked b14g, a Bitcoin staking app on Core, to withdraw zero tokens 99 times. Core's staking code read each one as "withdraw everything." About 70% of the coins had still not moved by that evening.

item.title: StandX cancels its token and shuts down. Users get one DUSD payout of unknown size
item.description: The perpetuals exchange on BNB Chain and Solana dropped its token plans, switched trading to close-only and opened a one-time DUSD airdrop claim on October 31, 2026. It has not said how big the pool is, and the claim closes on December 31.

item.title: Lisk shuts its chain October 31 and burns a quarter of LSK. Tokens left behind are lost
item.description: Lisk set October 31, 2026, as the last day of its own blockchain and its DAO. It is burning 100 million LSK, a quarter of supply, and is turning the token into a loyalty reward on Ethereum. Anything not bridged out in time is lost, the project says.

item.title: OKX's 48th reserve report shows $29.4 billion, up 27% in three months, with BTC at 110%
item.description: OKX marked four years of monthly proof-of-reserves reports on October 30. Its primary assets rose from $23.1 billion in July to $29.4 billion, and every listed coin is backed at least 1:1. Here is what the report proves and what it leaves out.

item.title: Polymarket repaid $3.9 million after a vendor's script turned on its users. What broke?
item.description: A hijacked performance-monitoring script on polymarket.com used logged-in sessions to sell positions and pull funds. Polymarket's postmortem says 95% of affected wallets are now fully refunded, and it paid $1.2 million more for losses during its trading pause.

item.title: Polymarket repays $3.9 million after a hacked vendor script hits it for the second time
item.description: On October 29, a compromised outside script on polymarket.com used logged-in sessions to sell positions and drain 726 wallets. Polymarket paused trading, repaid 689 of them in full within a day, and is covering pause losses too. It was the second vendor script attack in four months.

item.title: Four years after the Nomad Bridge hack, a man is extradited to the US over $2.89 million
item.description: Prosecutors say Alexander Gurevich ran four exploit transactions against the Nomad Bridge on August 1, 2022, taking 103 WBTC and 300 WETH. It is the second old DeFi exploit case to reach a US courtroom this month, three weeks after the Uranium Finance hacker's conviction was announced.

item.title: PREDICT sale done, trading on hold: Binance postpones Predict.fun's launch, no new date
item.description: The BNB Chain prediction market sold PREDICT on Binance Wallet on October 29, then Binance Alpha and spot trading were postponed hours before launch. The airdrop claim is frozen too, and nobody has said why.

item.title: Bitcoin hashrate is back above 1 zettahash: two difficulty jumps in 13 days
item.description: Mining difficulty rose 5.92% on October 16 and another 5.54% on October 29, ending seven months below the 1 ZH/s line. A new record is about 5% away, but miners earn far less per machine than a year ago.

item.title: Binance lost a record $6.3 billion. Who froze $2.7 billion of it?
item.description: Attackers emptied Binance's hot wallets on October 29 in the biggest crypto theft on record. Stablecoin issuers froze about $2.7 billion, the FBI blames North Korea, and Binance says users will not pay.

item.title: Coinbase made $719 million in Q3. Almost all of it came from its own crypto pile
item.description: Coinbase swung from a $359 million loss to a $719 million profit, but $715 million of that was a paper gain on crypto it holds. Retail spot trading volume fell 59% in a year, while prediction markets passed $200 million a year in revenue.

item.title: Strategy booked a record $20.9 billion profit. So why did it sell $432 million of bitcoin?
item.description: The biggest corporate bitcoin holder had its best quarter ever on paper. But each share is now backed by 3.7% less bitcoin than in January, it spent $2 billion propping up its own preferred stock, and its CFO is leaving.

item.title: Kalshi raises $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation. Can it outrun the states?
item.description: The prediction market says it now runs at more than $1 trillion in annualized volume and wants to sell perps, indices and compute markets. Two days earlier, its federal regulator sued Utah to stop the state from shutting such markets down.

item.title: Uniswap opens the tool behind its UNI burns to any app. Robinhood takes USDC instead
item.description: TJAR, the system that turns Uniswap's protocol fees into UNI and burns it, is now open to everyone. It handled more than $15.3 million in a month, and its first outside user wants stablecoins, not UNI.

item.title: NYSE owner ICE wants Hyperliquid perps in America. What stands in the way?
item.description: Intercontinental Exchange plans to run Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures markets for US retail traders with Trade[XYZ], and is taking a minority stake. HYPE jumped almost 20% on the day, but nothing goes live until US regulators approve it.

item.title: BNB Chain's Jenner hard fork walls off 5% of every block for payments. Who gets in?
item.description: Jenner went live on the BSC testnet on October 28, 2026. It reserves block space for payments, adds a native token standard with freeze and seizure powers, and gives smart contracts millisecond time. Mainnet has no date yet.

item.title: Ethos promised WHUF buyers 85% back. It has paid $1.6 million as the token halved
item.description: The reputation protocol on Base sold 20% of its token at $4.20 and guaranteed qualifying buyers $3.57. WHUF unlocked on October 8 and fell to about $1.93, so buyers are cashing in the floor while the Ethos Foundation burns the returned tokens.
